title: Black Tax: Understanding the financial transfers of the emerging black middle class
note: 2018. Publisher abstract; questionnaire of 118 people and six interviews in South Africa. Not a representative African diaspora survey or an app-impact study.

title: Remittance Prices Worldwide, Issue 54
note: Q3 2025 observations, accessed October 2026. Average cost of sending USD 200. Regional and service-type samples differ; these are not current individual quotes.

title: International money transfer homepage
note: Public marketing checked 5 October 2026. Documents love/family framing and speed claims; neither a service test nor evidence of psychological harm.

title: What are scheduled transfers?
note: Help documentation checked 5 October 2026. Describes frequency, end dates and execution-time exchange rates. Availability depends on account and currency.

title: 2025 Annual Report
note: Company filing for 2025. Explains transaction fees and foreign-exchange spreads. Establishes business incentives, not abusive intent.

title: Fourth quarter and full year 2025 results
note: 18 February 2026. Global company-reported send volume and revenue; not African remittances, family-support expenditure or household outcomes.

title: Remittance Responses to Temporary Discounts
note: September 2014 research paper. Randomised 10-week fee discounts for Salvadoran and Guatemalan migrants. Persistence observed up to 20 weeks after expiry; not a study of African app users.

title: Testing Commitment Devices for Remittances among Filipino Migrants in Rome
note: Research summary of a lab-in-the-field experiment and product take-up. The over-15% labeling result concerns experimental remittance choices, not an Africa-wide effect.

title: The Impacts of Labeling Remittances on Migrants and Their Households in the Philippines
note: 2018-2020 evaluation: 4,458 Filipino migrants in the UAE and 2,075 recipient households. Responses differed by baseline remittance activity.

title: Savings in Transnational Households: A Field Experiment
note: Study of Salvadoran transnational households. More migrant control raised savings at the partner bank; authors caution against assuming that control necessarily improves household welfare.

title: Beginners guide to asset allocation, diversification and rebalancing
note: General principles on horizon, risk and diversification. US source; does not establish local eligibility or tax treatment for African or diaspora investors.

title: Save for a rainy day
note: Emergency-savings guidance. Deposit protection and account eligibility must be checked in the actual jurisdiction; no US coverage rule is generalised here.

title: DhowCSD frequently asked questions
note: December 2025. Account-opening requirements and government-securities access. Auction notices control product-specific minimums and terms.

title: Licensees and approved schemes
note: Live regulatory directory checked 5 October 2026. Verify the exact legal entity and scheme; registration does not guarantee returns.

title: FGN Savings Bond subscription portal questions
note: Checked 5 October 2026. NGN 5,000 minimum, two- and three-year offerings, CSCS account and quarterly coupons. Incomplete tax answers on the portal were not relied upon.

title: Find a registered operator
note: Directory checked 5 October 2026. Authorisation is activity-specific; confirm the scheme and custody arrangements separately.

title: Licensed mutual funds
note: Directory checked 5 October 2026, including fund managers and custodians/trustees. A listing is not a return or liquidity guarantee.

title: Requirements and responsibilities of primary dealers and bond market specialists
note: Notice displayed 17 September 2026. Describes authorised wholesale-auction participation. Individuals should establish their own eligible access route with a regulated institution.

title: About RSA Retail Savings Bonds
note: Checked 5 October 2026. Eligible citizens/permanent residents need a valid South African identity number and a South African bank account. Product terms and early access differ.

organisation: Financial Sector Conduct Authority South Africa
title: Regulated entities
note: Checked 5 October 2026. Includes collective investment schemes and regulated intermediaries. Does not settle an individual investor's tax residency.

title: Collective investment funds (OPCVM)
note: Official fund information and listings checked 5 October 2026. Review the information document, asset class, dealing frequency and charges.

title: Instruction generale des operations de change 2026
note: 2026 rules, notably articles 170-173. Foreign-currency funding and supporting conditions matter for investment transfer rights; no blanket promise for all accounts.

title: Investing as an individual
note: Checked 5 October 2026. Government securities through securities accounts with approved UEMOA banks or SGIs; individual issue notices set terms.

title: How to invest in the BRVM
note: Official investor guidance checked 5 October 2026. Securities account and authorised intermediary required; SGIs trade listed securities.

title: Open Your Account in Egypt initiative for Egyptians working abroad
note: 26 October 2025 announcement. Selected embassy/consulate routes, identity documents and banking services; current participation and eligibility require confirmation.

title: Capital market investor information
note: Checked 5 October 2026. Licensed brokers and investment-fund managers; independent registration checks remain necessary.

title: Workplace pensions
note: UK guidance checked 5 October 2026. Illustrates employer contributions and pension features; not a universal rule for all destination countries.

title: Remittances nearly doubled in a decade to reach USD 729 billion in 2025
note: 14 September 2026 release. USD 728.6 billion in 2025 refers to all low- and middle-income countries, not Africa alone.
